advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Detect alias-vs-alias collisions (same alias declared by two routes, or twice within one route) in _check_duplicates.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:245: `if alias in name_set:` — only checks alias against canonical spellings
ABSENCE: no aggregation of aliases across routes and no check that the same alias string appears on more than one route or twice on one route
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:236: `names = [r.name for r in routes]` — includes retired routes
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:253-262: `_check_alias_retired` separately emits `alias_retired_collision` for the same alias
test tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py:test_alias_retired_collision_rejected only asserts one code is present, so the redundant double-finding is not caught
advisory.finding: validate() does not detect two distinct routes declaring the SAME alias, nor a duplicate alias within a single route's aliases tuple. _check_duplicates compares aliases only against canonical names (name_set), never against the set of all declared aliases, so an ambiguous alias-to-alias collision passes validation clean.
merged_from: An alias that collides with a RETIRED canonical spelling emits two findings — 'duplicate' (from _check_duplicates, whose name_set includes retired routes) and 'alias_retired_collision' (from _check_alias_retired) — for the same underlying condition.
advisory.suggested_fix: Accumulate all declared aliases across routes and yield a duplicate/ambiguous finding when the same alias string appears more than once (in addition to the alias-vs-canonical check).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `rebar._cli._DERIVED_POLICY_SETS` exists and equals the live router frozensets (zero delta), pinning the __init__.py shadow-census binding directly.
evidence: search_files for `_DERIVED_POLICY_SETS` under tests/ returned `(no matches)`
test_cli_registry.py asserts on `_registry.derive_policy_sets()` directly (line ~76) but never reads `_cli._DERIVED_POLICY_SETS`
advisory.finding: The new module-level attribute `_DERIVED_POLICY_SETS = _registry.derive_policy_sets()` added to `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (the concrete behavior this file's diff introduces) is never asserted by any test; only the standalone `derive_policy_sets()` function is exercised (via `test_derived_policy_sets_have_zero_shadow_delta`), so a regression that drops, renames, or breaks the `__init__`-level shadow-census binding would go undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor removes or misbinds the `_DERIVED_POLICY_SETS` assignment in __init__.py while the standalone function still works — no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: `from rebar import _cli; assert _cli._DERIVED_POLICY_SETS[name] == getattr(_cli, name)` for each census set name.
